newsitem.title: ITALY: BOI says lira at same level as '92 after ERM exit.
newsitem.headline: BOI says lira at same level as '92 after ERM exit.

text.p: The Italian lira has returned to the same effective rate it was at just after it was thrown out of the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) in 1992, the Bank of Italy said in a half yearly report.
It said the lira was also at more or less the same real rate as when the ERM was launched in 1979.

"The lira exchange rate has stabilised at a level which in real terms (that is based on producer prices) is equivalent to that immediately after the devaluation of 1992 and not dissimilar to that which prevailed in 1979, when the ERM was launched," the report said.

The Italian currency plummeted more than 50 percent against the German mark in the two years after its expulsion from the ERM, but has risen strongly in recent months. The government says it wants to put it back in the ERM by the end of the year.
The lira recently entered a trading range just above the 1,000 level against the mark. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
